function_question: How does nature coordinate big groups with no leader?

hero.name: Rosa and Pixel
hero.role: a 14-year-old coder and her robot friend

opening.text: There was a girl called Rosa, 14, who loved coding, and her best friend was a helpful robot called Pixel.
After school, Rosa and Pixel helped the crew at a drone light show, charging batteries and testing patterns.
The crew planned their biggest show yet: 100 drones. "If the main computer loses its signal," Pixel beeped, "they could all crash!" Rosa wondered: could the drones fly together with no leader at all?

card.problem: 100 drones must fly together without crashing and without a leader
card.goal: Write 3 simple rules that make a group move like a flock
card.rules: No leader. Each drone only sees its nearest neighbours.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The leaderless show

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Rosa and Pixel need a teammate

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The swarm heroes
chapters.line: You meet flocks, schools and swarms that have no boss.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the three rules

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Rosa and Pixel need 100 drones to fly together without crashing, and without a leader. Can you help them write the rules? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some coders already have a hunch about how swarms work. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature runs huge groups with no boss. Tap each card to meet four swarm heroes!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Predict first: after 5 rounds of your rules, will your paper drones be scattered or all facing one way?
guide.sketch: Draw your rules so clearly that a robot could follow them!
guide.build_and_test: Run the human flock: walk slowly with arms folded. First no rules, then your rules. Count every bump!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE number in ONE rule and count the collisions again.
guide.ending: And ever since then, Rosa and Pixel's drones have flown by your three rules, and the crowd gasps every time they swoop.

quick_check.question: 100 drones each watch their 7 nearest neighbours. How many neighbour-checks is that in one update?
quick_check.right: Right! 100 × 7 = 700. If every drone watched all 99 others, it would be 9,900 checks. That's why nature keeps it local!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Each of the 100 drones checks 7 neighbours, so multiply.

clue_cards.name: Starling
clue_cards.trick: Tracks only its 6 or 7 nearest neighbours.
clue_cards.does: Tens of thousands turn together, and no bird is in charge.

clue_cards.name: Fish school
clue_cards.trick: Feels its neighbours through sensors along its sides.
clue_cards.does: Keeps a gap, turns when they turn, and almost never crashes.

clue_cards.name: Ant
clue_cards.trick: Leaves scent trails on the ground.
clue_cards.does: Others follow the strongest trail: the message is in the environment.

clue_cards.name: Desert locust
clue_cards.does: Above about 70 per square metre, they line up and march one way.

predict.prompt: Leader or local rules? Predict first!

items.label: A marching band following its drum major
Cars keeping a safe gap on a motorway

predict.explain: A leader gives one order to everyone, but if the leader fails, everyone is lost. With local rules, each member reacts to its neighbours, so the group keeps working even if some members drop out.

lab.title: The paper swarm lab
lab.predict: Run 5 rounds on the grid. Which set of rules will get your 8 paper drones moving together with the fewest collisions?

tool.name: How Might We
tool.intro: How Might We turns what you learn about people into a hopeful question to design for. You find the User, their Need and a surprising Insight, then join them into one "How might we…?" question. Today you'll use all 4 parts.

parts.name: User
parts.example: 🥪 A kid who eats lunch in a busy canteen.
parts.starter: Our users are the show crew and…

parts.name: Need
parts.what: What do they need to do? Use a verb.
parts.example: 🥪 They need to open it with one hand while holding a tray.

parts.name: Insight
parts.what: What surprising thing did you learn?
parts.example: 🥪 Most lunchboxes have two stiff clips, so kids give up and wait for help.
parts.starter: The surprise is that a starling only watches…

parts.name: How might we…?
parts.what: Join them into one hopeful question.
parts.example: 🥪 How might we make a lunchbox that opens with one hand?
